findings.evidence: "The people operations office publishes the reimbursement log each quarter" versus "The benefits team publishes the reimbursement log after every open enrollment period"
findings.fix: Merge the two sections into one, name a single owner and a single publication cadence, and remove the duplicate "Overview" heading.
findings.location: "Program Overview" section, compared with the "Overview" section near the end of the document
findings.violation: The document names two different owners and two different schedules for what appears to be the same recurring publication, so a reader cannot tell which office or cadence actually applies.

findings.evidence: "Similarly, the IT asset group tracks the stipend budget each quarter. Staff can request a printed copy from the benefits team at any time."
findings.fix: Replace "Similarly" with a transition that reflects the actual relationship, or none at all, and state explicitly which document staff can request a printed copy of.
findings.violation: "Similarly" implies this sentence parallels the one before it, but tracking a budget internally is not similar to publishing a log externally, and it is unclear whether the printed copy on offer is a copy of the reimbursement log or of the budget tracking.

findings.evidence: "If the position counts as full-time, the stipend can apply. If the employee has completed 90 days of continuous service, the stipend can apply. If the request arrives before the benefit year ends, the stipend can apply. Only once every condition above is met does the home-office equipment stipend become available to the employee."
findings.fix: Combine the three conditions into one sentence joined by "and," for example: the stipend applies once the position is full-time, the employee has completed 90 days of continuous service, and the request arrives before the benefit year ends.
findings.violation: Each conditional sentence reads as independently sufficient for the stipend to apply, but the closing sentence says all three conditions are required together, so the paragraph contradicts itself about whether the conditions are joined by "or" or "and."

findings.evidence: "However, reimbursement is not available without a completed receipt."
findings.fix: Replace "However" with "In addition" or fold the receipt requirement directly into the eligibility list.
findings.violation: "However" signals a contrast with the preceding eligibility conditions, but a receipt requirement is an additional condition rather than a contrasting one, leaving the logical relationship between the paragraphs unclear.

findings.evidence: "Then, the review takes longer because the manager who normally handles it is traveling; the backup reviewer who covers for absences was not told that the request needs sign-off before the portal releases the confirmation email."
findings.fix: Split the sentence in two, state plainly whether the delay scenario is general policy or a one-time example, and clarify the timing of the sign-off relative to the confirmation email.
findings.violation: It is not clear whether "before the portal releases the confirmation email" modifies "was not told" or "needs sign-off," and it is unclear whether this describes a general rule or a single incident, since "Then" suggests it is a normal step in every request.

findings.evidence: "The manager confirms the equipment category matches the approved list."
findings.fix: Define or link to the approved equipment list where it is first mentioned.
findings.violation: "The approved list" is referenced as though already defined, but no approved equipment list appears anywhere earlier in the document.

findings.evidence: "The manager approves items pursuant to internal discretion, notwithstanding the standard review checklist."
findings.fix: State directly whether the checklist is mandatory or advisory, and list the required documents under this heading.
findings.violation: Saying approval happens by discretion "notwithstanding" the checklist leaves it unclear whether the checklist is actually used, and the section is titled "Required Documentation" but never states what documentation is required.

findings.evidence: "Also, the deposit happens in order to offset costs the employee already paid at this point in time."
findings.fix: Delete the sentence, or shorten it to "The deposit reimburses costs the employee already paid."
findings.violation: The sentence is filler that just restates that this is a reimbursement, and "at this point in time" is a wordy substitute for "now."

findings.evidence: "You must keep your equipment in good working condition and we may ask for a brief photo check once a year."
findings.fix: Rewrite in third person to match the rest of the document, for example: employees must keep equipment in good working condition, and the benefits team may request a brief photo check once a year.
findings.violation: The document uses third person everywhere else, but this sentence switches abruptly to second person, which is inconsistent with the surrounding text.

findings.evidence: "You record the stipend item on the request form. Finance reconciles the stipend item against the request log each month. Payroll releases the stipend item amount after that monthly review."
findings.fix: Define "stipend item" or replace it with "stipend," and reconcile the payout timing and responsible party with the "Reimbursement Amounts" section.
findings.violation: A section titled "Terminology Notes" is expected to define terms, but "stipend item" is never defined, the paragraph switches to second person again, and the described payout process, a monthly Payroll release, conflicts with the "Reimbursement Amounts" section's statement that the finance office deposits the amount within one pay cycle.

findings.evidence: "Also, you submit the request in the portal. You track its status there until the payment clears."
findings.fix: Remove this paragraph, and if status tracking is a genuinely new detail, add it to "How to Apply" instead.
findings.violation: This restates, in second person, information already given in third person in the "How to Apply" section, producing duplicated content under an unrelated heading.

findings.evidence: "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and uploading the receipt."
findings.fix: Merge "Request Steps" into "How to Apply" so the process is described in one place, in order.
findings.violation: This section is placed at the end of the document, far from the "How to Apply" section that already describes starting a request, splitting the single application process across two disconnected sections.

findings.evidence: "The team then routes the request to the correct approver based on department."
findings.fix: Use one consistent name for the approver role across sections, and explain how department-based routing relates to the manager and backup reviewer already described.
findings.violation: Routing based on department to an unnamed "correct approver" is not reconciled with the "How to Apply" section's mention of a specific manager who normally handles requests and a backup reviewer, leaving it unclear whether these are the same role.

findings.evidence: "The finance office reviews every stipend request over 200 dollars before it pays out."
findings.fix: State in "Approval Timeline" whether requests over 200 dollars require an additional finance review step and how it affects the stated timeline.
findings.violation: This introduces a dollar-based review step that is not mentioned in the "Approval Timeline" section, which states only that the request is reviewed within two business days by the manager, leaving it unclear whether the finance review is additional, sequential, or extends the stated timeline.

findings.evidence: "The benefits team publishes the vendor list each quarter."
findings.fix: Rename the heading to match the content, such as "Vendor List," or replace the content with the contact and update information the heading promises.
findings.violation: The heading promises information about questions or updates, such as who to contact, but the content instead introduces a vendor list that is never mentioned anywhere else in the document.
